cases.name: 20 реальных runtime

cases.evidence: Synthetic Core composition test twentyProfileRestoreStartupRegistrationSurvivesStallFailureRetryAndSelectionChanges passed locally 1/1 on 2026-10-13 and exact-SHA macOS CI run 38412386934 succeeded for test commit 5879143cc420cb0047606d099aa49810a609060e. It composes restore planning, parallelism=2 scheduling, route registration before first request, a stalled profile, failed first request and fresh-generation retry, then routes all 20 client updates while selected account changes. This verifies Core contracts only: it does not invoke AppDelegate.restoreProfiles/openProfileWhileHoldingStartupPermit, real TDLib, real accounts, or same-Mac resource/performance behavior. APP01 remains partial. Current source 94740d3 also passes the focused synthetic test twentyProfileRestoreStartupRegistrationSurvivesStallFailureRetryAndSelectionChanges under Xcode 27 / Swift 6.4; this still does not invoke AppDelegate restoreProfiles or real TDLib/accounts. Local test strengthening: `twentyProfileRestoreStartupRegistrationSurvivesStallFailureRetryAndSelectionChanges` now uses the exact `AccountRestorePlanner.enqueueStartupProfiles` fan-out helper called by production `restoreProfiles()`, asserting all 20 profiles are synchronously queued before exercising the bounded scheduler, one stalled open, one failed first request, retry with a fresh generation, pre-request route registration, and A/B selection isolation. Focused local test passed 1/1 under arm64 / Xcode 27 / Swift 6.4; no real Telegram accounts or runtime were used. Exact-source hosted macOS suite passed 160/160 in run 38493619014 for test/checkpoint commit bb9b38f8abee386b83b9f7949b22b6cfcc985744; app-source commit remained 2d8a4e5964211c9fbd40136f5470da7d47266937. cases.name: Запуск без head-of-line blocking
cases.expected: Ошибка ключа, отсутствие сети или reauth A не блокирует запуск остальных; не появляется второй DB owner.
cases.evidence: At app-source 26abae365b4eec54882ae69cc1274e20ddabb276, AppDelegate calls the production-used ProfileStoragePreparer before TDLib runtime creation. Two targeted local tests passed: one injected errSecInteractionNotAllowed among 20 synthetic scheduled profiles; the failed profile retained its existing DB/draft files and no replacement key was added while the other 19 prepared. Exact-SHA macOS CI 38425731506 and pinned TDLib/Dev.app assembly 38425731851 passed. This does not test actual macOS Keychain lock/ACL behavior, a stalled real SecItem call in AppDelegate orchestration, login, or 20 authorized sessions; APP02 remains partial. Current implementation replaces the global serial Keychain executor with OperationQueue(maxConcurrentOperationCount: 2), keeping blocking SecItem work bounded while allowing another account to prepare its keys if one operation stalls. The corrected focused test stalled operation 1, confirmed operation 2 entered and completed its own work path, confirmed operation 3 waited for a slot, then verified operation 3 advanced after release. Local Xcode 27 / Swift 6.4 focused test passed 1/1; exact-source macOS Swift run 38487262779 and pinned-TDLib Dev.app/lifecycle run 38487262804 passed; metadata run 38487262753 passed. This remains synthetic executor coverage, not an actual macOS SecItem stall, 20 authorized accounts, or an appDelegate restore measurement. New combined 20-profile regression `oneStalledProfileKeychainPreparationDoesNotBlockTheOtherNineteen` uses the same `RuntimeStartupScheduler`, `SecretsStore.performKeychainOperation`, and `ProfileStoragePreparer` as startup. It leaves one profile blocked while the other 19 finish preparation, then releases the blocker and confirms all permits drain. Local focused test passed 1/1 on arm64 / Xcode 27.0 / Swift 6.4 (compile 17.99 s, test 0.018 s). Hosted exact-source CI is pending; this remains synthetic and does not establish OS Keychain, AppDelegate lifecycle, real-account, or 20-runtime coverage. Follow-up commit 67341ba includes the combined APP02 synthetic stall regression and exact-source CI 38504170791 passed 164/164; this still does not prove SecItem, AppDelegate restore, authorized sessions, or 20-runtime operation.

cases.name: Lock при startup/reauth

cases.evidence: At app-source commit 0fe2a13ecd7f227e10a2c1fa6773069c53f83e52, lock() now closes PrivacyDispatchBarrier before UI cleanup or draft storage I/O. This makes command dispatch linearize before the lock or be rejected after it, including while dirty drafts flush. Local Swift suite passed 126/126, including privacyLockWaitsForAnAtomicDispatchAndRejectsTheNextIntent and privacyBarrierRejectsQueuedAuthenticationAfterLockAndUnlock. Exact-source macOS CI 38379269975 and pinned TDLib/isolated Dev.app workflow 38379269906 succeeded. Source review confirms restoreProfiles is independent of lockState and locked authorization updates retain current state without presenting auth UI; LocalAuthentication cancellation keeps the UI locked. Native startup-under-lock, reauth UI on a real profile, and concurrent background-account behavior remain unverified; acceptance stays partial. At current app-code commit 477404afd89378affb9cc21eb6c0e32745cb5091, source review confirms profile restoration/start scheduling has no Privacy Lock early exit; routed auth updates continue through each LocalAccountRuntime.consume, while the selected UI handler returns before presenting an interactive auth step when lockState is true. After successful LocalAuthentication, unlock presents the selected runtime's current authorization state. This confirms code structure only; real reauth and multi-account runtime behavior remain unverified.

cases.name: Шумный аккаунт
cases.expected: Burst не создаёт бесконечные UI/tasks/фото queues и не теряет edit/delete/auth/TTL; foreground B остаётся отзывчивым.
cases.evidence: At app-source commit e89265c0dda7dc88a7d7a7f75abd5010c25a48c9, TDLibUpdateBuffer adds a hard-bounded overflow reserve: at most one event for each of 20 client lanes, one unrouteable lane, and additional reserved bytes capped at 25% of the primary byte budget. A later audit found that one event larger than byteCapacity could still enter an otherwise empty queue. Fix 6c6fff49d6c43746b3990de178b723d1eaf75172 rejects oversized queue events and closes the receive gateway with an explicit error; the C bridge checks a 16 MiB maximum before copying TDLib's borrowed buffer. Added regression tests cover rejection while empty and fail-closed/send rejection. The exact-source local suite passed 136/136; macOS CI 38395900507 and pinned TDLib/Dev.app workflow 38395900428 succeeded on the same SHA. Instruments, real 20-account burst, queue/task/RSS behavior under load, and native foreground responsiveness remain unverified; acceptance stays partial.

cases.name: Фото
cases.expected: Реальные read/send/caption; huge/corrupt decode bounded; album context; picker A не отправляет B.
cases.evidence: Photo pipeline, album grouping, bounded decode, staged-send and manifest regressions remain in the 80/80 exact-source suite for fe39bc1bd7141fb5b9c1ea706cdc1c06d357e63a. This does not prove real-account photo delivery or memory-pressure behavior; status stays partial. Static review found that the current v1.8.68 TDLib schema requires `openMessageContent` when photo content is actually opened, but the AppKit full-size photo viewer did not issue it. The viewer now sends that request only after the full-size image is successfully decoded and presented; the call is bound to the selected account, expected Telegram identity, runtime generation, and privacy epoch through PrivacyDispatchBarrier. Final exact-worktree serial suite passed 151/151 in 0.207 seconds; AppKit/Core build completed in 5.33 seconds on Xcode 27 / Swift 6.4. Exact hosted CI, pinned Dev.app compile/smoke, and real-account photo interaction remain pending; APP20 stays partial. Test-only deterministic cache injection prevents scoped delete assertions from depending on NSCache retention under system memory pressure; production continues to use NSCache.
